regions.speciality: bespoke men's tailoring; Savile Row described as 'the undisputed international center of bespoke tailoring' until the 1960s (Hong Kong tailors page) and home of the New Bespoke Movement
Harris Tweed: handwoven by islanders, finished and spun in the Outer Hebrides; definition protected by the Harris Tweed Act 1993 and the Orb Mark
bespoke suits, 'well-known for producing bespoke men's clothing', once the claimed world capital of bespoke suiting; fly-in travelling tailors

authentic kente weaving; towns noted for kente weaving: Bonwire, Sakora Wonoo, Ntonso, Safo, Adawomase; 'kente brands led by master weavers are in high demand'; kente prints by Vlisco and Akosombo Textile Ltd
Dutch wax / African wax prints; Vlisco Group owns Vlisco, Uniwax, Woodin and GTP; African makers include ABC Wax and Akosombo Textiles
haute couture; Paris became the centre of the industry from the mid-nineteenth century; term protected by French law, Chambre Syndicale de la Couture Parisienne
luxury and tailored fashion; Milan ranked top fashion capital in 2009 (Global Language Monitor, per page); 1950s Florence soirees by Giorgini let the 'Italian school' compete with French couture
revival of traditional weaving, printing, dyeing and embroidery (ikat, patola, bandhani, shisha) by organisations, NGOs and designers
lopapeysa wool sweaters; Alafoss is the most historic Icelandic wool factory (since 1896) and main lopi producer
Norwegian knitwear; Dale of Norway renowned since 1956 for official Olympic ski-team sweaters, Devold (1853), Oleana
Aran sweaters; Inis Meáin still makes them in the traditional hand-finished way on the Aran islands (GQ); Aran Crafts 'largest Aran producer'

Shetland and Fair Isle knitwear (Jamieson's of Shetland, only business taking Shetland wool from fleece to finished knitwear in the Isles); Highland dress and kilts (Kinloch Anderson, Royal Warrants since 1934)
selvedge denim: 'Okayama prefecture, where denim factories have been turning out high-quality selvedge denim for decades using 1940s shuttle looms'; Japan described as 'denim promised land'
kimono and Nishijin weaving: Kyoto's kimono regarded among Japan's finest; Nishijin textiles origin 5th century
Banarasi and Kanchipuram handloom sarees woven by master weavers
Istanbul named a fashion capital; Turkey a leading textile exporter; Vakko and Beymen founded by Atıl Kutoğlu

the Moroccan caftan, a symbol of national identity over eight centuries, listed on UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage (Dec 2025); Morocco named by UNESCO fashion report as supportive environment for local brands
indigo dyeing (adire), aso oke, bogolan mud cloth, ankara; Benin, Cameroon, Guinea, Nigeria renowned for indigo styles (UNESCO fashion report)
Tracht: dirndl and Lederhosen
wool, outback and surf clothing brands per Wikipedia category (79 brands); International Woolmark Prize is Australian Merino wool
Panama (toquilla straw) hats; Montecristi produces the finest Panamas
the Basque/French beret, made at Laulhère since 1840, EPV-labelled; Béarn the origin of the beret
leather glove-making; Millau 'known as the Glove Capital', artisans mastering leathercraft for centuries; Causse listed among UNESCO 'Métiers d'Art Rares' and EPV
leather gloves; Saint-Junien 'also known as The City of the Leather Glove'
glove-making since the 18th century; Pécs Glove Factory once 3,000 workers; artisanal revival brands
guayaberas, hipiles and ternos; Kimbilá 'one of Yucatán's best places to shop for handcrafted clothing', around 30 workshops
alpaca and vicuña garments; Grupo Inca founded in Arequipa to commercialise alpaca fibre
hand-woven silk ikat (atlas, adras) for national dress; Margilan 'considered a center of silk production'
ak-kalpak white felt hat craftsmanship (UNESCO Representative List 2019), felt garments
aso-oke hand-woven on narrow looms; Iseyin 'considered the home of aso-oke'
habesha kemis and zuria; Shiromeda 'one of Addis Ababa's most recognized destinations for Ethiopian clothing'
hand-made pollera (national dress); San José de Las Tablas artisans, Festival del Tambor y la Pollera, planned Ruta de la Pollera
backstrap-loom huipiles of Tzotzil, Tzeltal and Ikoot weavers
haute-couture caftan and takchita; the Caftan show (Femmes du Maroc) as launch platform; Tamy Tazi credited with reinventing the caftan

regions.speciality: Bonwire 'the leading centre of kente weaving in Ashanti', community workshop and village shops
